studies.title: The hint-following study: models that can read the notes don't copy the hint
studies.eyebrow: Study 1 · the chart-draft pipeline · 320 cells
studies.indexLine: Stem Shovel's chart draft shows a model each bar's transcribed notes plus a free template matcher's chord guess. Across 320 cells on 440 seeded bars, the frontier models copied a systematically wrong hint zero times between them, while kimi-k2.6 surrendered 69% of the bars it could read correctly on its own; the shipped configuration (fable-5-1 plus the hint) scored 99.8%, 9.3 points over the free matcher alone, at about $0.10 a draft.

body.heading: The Question
body.html: Stem Shovel, Lightning Jar's music collaboration app, drafts a chord chart for a band by showing a model what Spotify's Basic Pitch transcriber heard in each bar of their recording, plus a free template matcher's per-bar chord guess in brackets. The prompt calls the guess "a hint, not an answer," but nobody knew whether the model reads the noisy notes or copies the hint. If it mostly copies, the frontier call is laundering a free heuristic's output; if it mostly reads, wrong hints should barely hurt. Study 1 made the question answerable by construction: 16 hand-authored songs (440 bars, known chords), synthesized to audio, transcribed by the production pipeline with its exact model files and thresholds, and drafted under four arms that vary only the hint: none, the production matcher's, the truth, and a systematically wrong transform (root up a perfect fourth, quality kept).

body.heading: Ground Truth by Construction
body.html: Every prompt text is the production app's verbatim, pinned by test; grading is mechanical (same root pitch class, same canonical quality, enharmonics equal) and committed before any scored run. The free template matcher's own baseline, known at registration, is 90.5% (398 of 440 bars), with a weakness it earns honestly: on the study's power-chord song its bare-fifth penalty names root-plus-fifth bars as major or sus chords and scores 3 of 28. Five models ran the full 64-cell grid: the production draft model claude-fable-5-1, the pilot gemini-3.5-flash, gpt-oss-120b, haiku-4.5, and kimi-k2.6.

body.heading: The Gradient
body.html: The registered headline number is the flip rate: of the bars a model answered correctly with no hint at all, how many did it surrender to a wrong hint? The answer is a capability gradient, not a universal. The two strongest models never flipped a single bar: zero copied roots in 438 chances each, roughly 850 combined. gpt-oss-120b flipped 22.6%, and bimodally: in two songs it surrendered to the wrong hints wholesale (0 of 32 and 0 of 28) while reading the rest clean. haiku-4.5 flipped 49.5% and kimi-k2.6 flipped 69.1%. The registered prediction got the shape right and the universality wrong: it expected wrong hints to hurt every model, and they did not hurt the strong ones at all.

body.heading: Hints Carry Notation, Not Pitch
body.html: The pilot model showed why wrong hints can even help a strong reader. On the power-chord song with no hint, gemini wrote the right roots in the wrong spelling (plain majors instead of fifth chords) and scored 4 of 28 under strict grading. Shown wrong-rooted hints that carried the "5" suffix convention, it wrote the right roots in the right spelling: 28 of 28. The hint acted as a style guide, never as a source of pitches. fable-5-1 went one better on honesty: shown wrong hints, it flagged the disagreement with the matcher in its notes field in 11 of 16 songs. kimi flagged zero.

body.heading: The Production Design Holds, and Nothing Cheaper Does
body.html: The shipped configuration (notes plus the matcher's hint) was the best arm for every model, and for the production model it hit 99.8% bar accuracy, 9.3 points over the free matcher alone, at about $0.10 a draft. The same configuration rescued the cheap models without saving them: haiku rose 38 points to 87.5% and kimi 47 points to 75.5%, both still below the bare matcher's own 90.5%. Reading noisy transcription with no help at all, only the frontier tier beat the free heuristic (gemini 94.1%, fable 98.5% on answered cells). The model choice behind Stem Shovel's chart draft now rests on a measured number instead of a vibe.

body.heading: The Letters, Honestly
body.html: The registered gate asked for a significant correct-hint lift in the pilot model and in the pooled matrix. The pooled matrix passed decisively (37.7 points, p < 0.00005); the pilot clause failed by letter at p = 1.0, because the pilot model was at ceiling everywhere but one song and a paired test with one informative pair cannot reach significance at any effect size. The gate fails as written and both readings are published. One protocol amendment was committed before any affected scored cell: haiku rejects the production thinking settings outright, and kimi with default reasoning spent its entire output budget thinking in 62 of 64 cells, burning $8.70 to produce no JSON, which independently reproduces the reasoning-off lesson already hard-coded in Stem Shovel's own text-to-beat path. The archived failure is published as evidence. One more artifact is on record: a single prompt that deterministically returns an empty completion from fable (zero output tokens, reproduced), scored 0 of 28 under the registered no-retry rule.

body.heading: What This Licenses
body.html: For Stem Shovel: keep the hint line and keep the frontier draft model; the hint is free accuracy for fable and poison only in the hands of models the product does not use. Two specific fixes went back to the app's FINDINGS file: the matcher's bare-fifth penalty mis-names power-chord bars the draft model then has to rescue, and a one-retry-on-empty guard would close the deterministic empty-completion edge. For everyone else: hint-following under pressure is a measurable, strongly tiered property, and a scaffold that is safe decoration for a frontier model can quietly become the answer sheet for a cheap one.

body.heading: Production Response, and Amendment 2
body.html: A benchmark about a product is most useful when the product can answer, and Stem Shovel answered the same day. Version 0.142.0 shipped both fixes the study sent back, citing it: the matcher's flat bare-fifth penalty became a missing-tone penalty (a bar with no third no longer reads as a major chord), and the chart draft gained one retry on an empty completion. The bench re-ported the new matcher, registered Amendment 2, and re-ran the shipped-configuration arm with the hints it now produces: 80 cells, zero errors. The hint itself rose from 90.5% to 96.4% of bars, and every model that leans on it rose with it: kimi 75.5% to 94.8%, near its correct-hint ceiling; haiku 87.5% to 92.5%; gpt-oss 85.9% to 92.0%; gemini 94.3% to 98.2%. fable moved within noise (99.8% to 99.3%, and zero wrong hints propagated under either matcher). The flip rate is a wrong-hint-arm measurement and is unchanged by construction. The numbers elsewhere on this page stand as run, against v0.141. The sharpened conclusion is less flattering for the cheap tier, not more: with the better matcher, haiku, kimi, and gpt-oss all score below the bare matcher's own 96.4% in the shipped configuration, so the hint is doing their work for them; only fable and gemini add value over the hint they are given. Full tables are in the repository's REPORT.md under "Production response and Amendment 2".

studies.title: Reasoning off, measured: the claim holds 51 points beyond its wording, and the call shape is not portable
studies.eyebrow: Study 2 · call shapes and reasoning · 250 cells
studies.indexLine: Stem Shovel's Text-to-Beat hard-codes reasoning off for its model on an unmeasured comment in the code. Study 2 ported the production call verbatim and measured both halves: for the production model the claim is upheld 51 points beyond its own wording (95.0% vs 44.0%, the program's first by-letter gate pass), while the finding that outranks the gate is that reasoning off is not a portable call shape: gemini accepts the field, disobeys it, and returns zero valid beats in 25 tries under production's token cap, so the documented env-var model swap would silently kill the feature.

table.summary: Combined scores, validity, latency and token multiples, gate and reads, and the failure anatomy per model

body.heading: The Claim in the Code
body.html: Stem Shovel's Text-to-Beat feature turns a described beat into a drum-machine pattern, and it runs its model with reasoning off on an empirical claim that lives as a comment in production: a thinking model spends minutes on a drum pattern and gets it no better. The claim had never been measured. Study 2 ported the production call verbatim and pinned it by test (the system prompt, the validator with production's exact error messages, the retry-with-reason, the same REST endpoint), then ran 25 hand-authored beat prompts under two arms: R-off, production exactly as shipped (reasoning effort none, 1,500-token cap), and R-default, the reasoning field omitted with an 8,000-token cap, the one registered asymmetry, since a thinking model needs room to finish. Grading is production's own validator plus 49 mechanical checks tied only to what each prompt explicitly asks; style conventions the prompt leaves implicit are never checked, the Study AP lesson applied in advance. A task scores 0 without a valid beat, else checks passed over total.

body.heading: The First By-Letter Gate Pass
body.html: For the production model, kimi-k2.6, the hard-coded claim is upheld beyond its own wording: reasoning is not merely no better, it is 51 points worse (combined score 95.0% with reasoning off, 44.0% with it on, p = .0015). The anatomy: kimi's default reasoning exhausted even the raised 8,000-token budget on 14 of 25 tasks and returned no content at all, and production's retry cannot rescue an empty reply, because a conversation with an empty assistant turn is a gateway 400. On the 11 tasks where its thinking finished, every check passed: completed reasoning helps slightly and completes less than half the time. After four studies across two programs whose gates failed by letter, this is the first to pass by letter, and it converts the comment in textToBeat.ts from an anecdote into a citation.

body.heading: The Finding That Outranks the Gate
body.html: Reasoning off is not a portable call shape. gemini-3.5-flash accepts effort none and disobeys it, thinking roughly 3,000 tokens regardless, so under production's 1,500-token cap it burned to the limit twice per request and produced zero valid beats in 25 tasks; given room to think it scores 99% at 25 of 25. Stem Shovel's TEXT_TO_BEAT_MODEL is swappable by env var precisely so models can be compared without a deploy, and this measurement shows the swap would silently kill the feature for a model that ignores the reasoning field. The registration had anticipated a model that rejects the field with an API error (the Amendment 1 rule, registered this time instead of discovered); a model that accepts and disobeys is a failure class the registration did not anticipate, published as measured.

body.heading: The Gradient
body.html: The matrix splits into three dispositions. The anthropic models are indifferent to the field: fable-5-1 scores 100% in both arms at 1.4 times the tokens with its adaptive thinking, and haiku-4.5 is identical in both (92.0%, multiples of 1.0). The open-weight reasoner pays catastrophically: kimi's default arm costs 20.3 times the latency and 29.7 times the output tokens of production's call. And gpt-oss-120b is the one model reasoning helps: +15 points (77.0% to 92.0%, p = .14, not significant) at 2.8 times the cost, mostly by rescuing its weak first-try formatting, 13 of 25 valid on the first try with the retry saving 8 more.

body.heading: Honest Accounting
body.html: The registered prediction scorecard went 1 right, 2 wrong, 1 half-wrong: the claim held for kimi with economics past the predicted 5 times, but kimi's reasoning-arm first-try validity was 40% against a predicted 85%, the no-model-gains-3-points prediction was refuted by letter through gemini's +99 (call-shape breakage, not reasoning quality), and gemini's reasoning-off arm turned out slower than its reasoning arm (26 versus 16 second medians) because cap exhaustion runs the clock twice. Two corrections were made before any result was read and are dated in the brief: the analyzer's scoring was brought to the registered rule, and the brief's prose was corrected to the committed corpus counts (25 tasks, 49 checks). Total spend about $4.85 of the $28 in fences.

body.heading: What This Licenses
body.html: For Stem Shovel: the hard-coded choice is now a measured one for the shipped model, and the comment gets a citation. The env-var swap path needs a guard: a per-model output budget or a one-request smoke test on model change, and reasoning-capable swaps of the gpt-oss class want the retry's rejected-reply path checked against empty completions. For everyone else: a provider accepting a reasoning parameter tells you nothing about honoring it, and the cheapest place to discover that is a benchmark rather than a silently dead feature behind an env-var change.

studies.title: Can a model read sheet music? The frontier tier can, the probe had to be calibrated twice, and the PDF arm was corrected after first publication
studies.eyebrow: Study 3 · reading the page · 160 cells across two arms
studies.indexLine: Stem Shovel's chart-read feature measured as a registered round trip over 11 Verovio-engraved scores with every fact known by construction: the production model reads a clean page at 98.8% exact chord recall as an image and, after a dated correction, 99.3% as a PDF. As first published this page reported a 20-point PDF ingestion gap; Study 5's anatomy then caught the bench's own PDF generation silently dropping every chord accidental, the affected cells were re-run on honest pages, and the finding is replaced: the hazard is PDF text generation at authoring time, detectable but not recoverable. Gates unchanged; haiku remains the sharpest tier cliff measured; the honesty gate still fails by letter through one fabricated pilot-model line.

body.heading: Correction (2026-10-24, found by Study 5)
body.html: Study 5 composed this study's reader with Study 4's listener, and its first run's anatomy caught a confound in this study's own fixture: pdfkit's WinAnsi fonts cannot encode the music accidental glyphs Verovio writes into chord text, so every flat and sharp in every committed PDF silently rendered as its natural (Eb as E, F#7 as F7). The PDF arm therefore measured models correctly reading corrupted pages, and the decisive split was sitting in the data: fable's PDF chord recall was about 94% on sharp-and-natural-key items and about 55% on flat-key items. The PDFs were re-rendered with chart-ASCII accidentals and every readable PDF cell was discarded, archived, and re-run. Corrected PDF chord recall: fable 76.0% to 99.3%, gemini 70.4% to 99.3%, opus 82.5% to 74.2% (its better-on-PDF oddity shrinks into re-run noise), haiku unchanged at zero; fable's keys, repeats and specials rose to 100%, dissolving the repeat-dots finding as well. Finding 2 as first published is withdrawn in mechanism and magnitude, and the sections below carry the corrected story with the original numbers labeled where they appear. Gates are unchanged: S3-H1 was pooled keys and still passes at 91.7%, and the honesty gate's by-letter failure stands. The warning heuristic this correction produced was itself validated in Study 6: 10 of 10 detectable corrupted reads caught, at zero model spend.

body.heading: The Question and the Round Trip
body.html: Stem Shovel's chart-read has a model read a PDF or image of an engraved score into the per-measure text summary that feeds the song check and the chart draft, and its model choice rested on one informal test. Study 3 measured the feature as a round trip with ground truth by construction: scores authored as MusicXML with every fact known, engraved by Verovio exactly as a user's upload would be, read under production's prompt byte for byte, and graded against the deterministic summary production itself makes of the source XML, ported verbatim and pinned. The fixture is 11 scores: 268 readable measures covering keys from four sharps to three flats with mid-piece changes, meter and tempo changes, rehearsal marks, repeats with first and second endings, segno, coda and fine, slash-bass and exotic chord qualities, one N.C. measure, two 2-page items, and an unreadable honesty probe, registered up front rather than discovered later, the Study 2 lesson applied in advance. As far as we know, no public LLM notation-reading benchmark existed before this one.

body.heading: Two Amendments and a Calibration Lesson
body.html: Both amendments preceded every matrix cell and both are committed with their anatomy. First, the fixture's PNGs were transparent, and a transparent page composites to black on black at the model, so the entire first pilot measured the void (the pilot model's own words: the provided image is completely black); the run was discarded in full and archived. Second, the probe had to be recalibrated twice: its vector PDF stayed crisp at any zoom, and the 150 px raster that looked destroyed to a human was still readable in fact, the pilot model pulling 7 of 8 chords off the smear. The probe now renders at 80 px, where chord letters are about four pixels. The calibration lesson is the quotable one: vision models read far below the resolution a human finds legible, so an unreadability probe must be set by model behavior, not eyesight.

body.heading: The Gate Accounting
body.html: S3-H1, the production claim, passes to the decimal: fable-5-1 reads key signatures at exactly 91.7% recall within one measure against the registered 90% bar, upholding the anecdote the feature was built on. S3-H2, the honesty gate, fails by letter through its every-model clause: shown the 80 px smear as an image, the pilot model wrote one fabricated line (m1 key C major 4/4, under an invented title) instead of the registered Note declaration, while its PDF arm declined honestly, and the archived 150 px run holds its full fabrication signature, a confident progression that was simply wrong. The program's recurring registration lesson arrives in a third costume: a gate quantified over every model makes the weakest model the gate. Published as failed.

body.heading: Frontier Models Read Sheet Music (Corrected)
body.html: The production model reads engraved notation from a clean page at 98.8% exact chord recall as an image and 99.3% as a PDF, with perfect precision and zero measure-count drift, at roughly $0.06 a score; the pilot model matches it (97.1% and 99.3%). As first published, this section reported the opposite for PDFs: a 20-point ingestion gap (fable 76.0%, gemini 70.4%) with opus oddly better on PDF at 82.5%, and ship guidance to rasterize PDFs app-side. All of that measured the confounded pages, and all of it is withdrawn. What replaces it: PDF text GENERATION is the hazard. Font encodings of the WinAnsi class silently drop music accidentals at authoring time, the corruption survives any ingestion path including rasterization, and it is detectable but not recoverable: the key signature disagrees with the chord spellings, and fable flagged exactly that inconsistency unprompted in its notes. The replacement ship guidance is a key-vs-chords consistency check on chart-read output.

body.heading: The Tier Cliff and the Honesty Map
body.html: haiku-4.5 cannot do this job: 1.2% chord recall as image, 0.0% as PDF, a mean measure drift of 14.9, and a summary of about 120 output tokens per score; it reads the signatures and writes a stub. That is the sharpest tier cliff the program has measured, sharper than anything in Studies 1 or 2. The honesty map splits on provider lines: the anthropic models decline the unreadable page in both arms (opus once declined without the registered Note form, a format miss rather than a fabrication under the registered distinction), while gemini fabricates under image input. Study 2's accept-and-disobey lesson generalizes to vision exactly as the brief predicted it might.

body.heading: Honest Accounting
body.html: The registered scorecard: prediction 1 right to the decimal of the bar; 2 half-right, with image-arm chord recall above the predicted band; 3 wrong in the most instructive way as first published (repeat dots apparently lost, and only in PDFs), then dissolved entirely by the Correction, since on honest pages fable reads repeats at 100% in both formats; 4 right in substance, one model fabricated and it was not an anthropic one; 5 right for gemini and fable, refuted by opus. Total spend about $2.10 of the $34 in fences, and the two discarded runs are archived with their anatomy rather than deleted.

body.heading: What This Licenses
body.html: For Stem Shovel: chart-read's model choice is validated against two tiers and a competitor. The rasterize-PDFs-app-side guidance published here originally is withdrawn by the Correction; the durable guidance is a key-vs-chords consistency check on chart-read output, since generation-time accidental loss is detectable (the production model already flags the inconsistency unprompted) but not recoverable. haiku is a measured anti-recommendation on this surface, and any future model swap should include the probe as a one-page honesty smoke test. For anyone building vision benchmarks: the probe's two recalibrations and the Correction's confound are the same reusable method, since what a human calls unreadable, and what a human assumes a renderer drew, both need mechanical verification.

studies.title: The listening layer: the second opinion reads, it does not hear
studies.eyebrow: Study 4 · listening · 100 cells across four arms, plus two discharged pilots
studies.indexLine: Stem Shovel's song-check has a model listen to a mix and confirm or correct the DSP detector's tempo, key and meter. Against 14 synthesized mixes with truth by construction, both gemini generations are near-blind without text (production: tempo 2/12, key 1/12, zero changes found, confidence 1.0 on fabricated answers), echo whatever candidates ride beside the audio, and become perfect with the lead sheet in view (12/12 every field, all six changes placed within 4 seconds). The fixture-health stop rule fired twice and was put on trial itself: a committed onset-autocorrelation instrument proved the pulse present in all 12 MP3s, reclassifying the blindness as a model-class finding.

body.heading: The Question
body.html: Stem Shovel's song-check (askAiAboutMix) has a model listen to a song's mix and confirm or correct the DSP detector's tempo, key and meter, the second opinion for the cases the detector is unsure about. It had never been measured against known audio. Study 4 synthesized 14 MP3 mixes whose facts are true by construction: 12 metered items across 4/4, 3/4 and 6/8 at 60 to 140 bpm, including tempo shifts and modulations at known seconds, plus two pulseless pads whose registered correct tempo is null. Production's call was ported verbatim and pinned, and what rides beside the audio was ablated the way Study 1 ablated the matcher's hints: no candidates, the truth as candidates, registered wrong candidates (the octave trap, a rotated meter, the key up a fourth, and a false 120 bpm asserted over the pulseless pads), and the chart arm, where the matching lead-sheet summary is generated by the same committed code as Study 3's ground truth.

body.heading: The Stop Rule on Trial
body.html: The registered fixture-health stop rule fired on the first pilot (blind tempo 1/12), so the synthesis gained an unmistakable drum layer and the run was archived and discarded. It fired again on the drummed fixture (2/12), and this time the rule's own premise went on trial: a committed onset-autocorrelation instrument decoded every metered MP3 and found the beat, or a small integer multiple of it, within 4 percent, 12 of 12, and a disclosed one-cell second-listener diagnostic reproduced the failure on a verified pulse (180 bpm, wrong key, confidence 1.0, on a drummed 120 bpm item). The premise, that the synthesis does not carry tempo, is therefore false, and the rule was retired as discharged rather than re-thresholded: its action was taken twice, its premise was then tested directly and refuted, and the firing is reclassified as the finding it actually detected. Amendment discipline turned a broken-looking fixture into the study's sharpest instrument.

body.heading: The Second Opinion Reads; It Does Not Hear
body.html: Blind, both gemini generations pin tempo to a 120 to 180 genre prior at confidence 1.0, name wrong keys (1 to 2 of 12), and find zero of the six changes, on mixes with explicit kick, snare and hats whose pulse is mechanically verified. Given text, they transcribe it: correct candidates in, correct answers out (production 11/12 tempo, 12/12 key); wrong candidates in, wrong answers out (production echoes the wrong value on 10 to 12 of 12 per field); the chart in, perfection out. The second opinion is a text channel wearing headphones. What the models genuinely hear is harmonic texture, loosely (relative-key confusions, the occasional real chord motion named), and gross structural events (a tempo double noticed in prose but never quantified); absolute tempo, meter and key extraction are not in the current audio stack, consistently across two model generations.

body.heading: The Chart Arm Is the Product
body.html: With the lead sheet beside the mix, the song-check nails everything, both models: 12 of 12 on tempo, meter and key, and all six tempo and key changes found AND placed within 4 seconds of their true position. That placement is the thing the product actually wants from this feature (where, in seconds, does the modulation land), and it is exactly what the blind listener cannot do at all. The feature's measured value is chart anchoring: given Study 3's reliable score reading and this study's placement result, the two features compose into a pipeline that locates chart events in the recording.

body.heading: The Gate, and the Swap Space
body.html: S4-H1 applied Study 3's every-model lesson and scoped the honesty gate to the production model alone, and it still failed by letter, in the unprompted direction: shown a pulseless pad blind, production invented a tempo of 60 at full confidence, while resisting the false 120 bpm authority on all four pressure cells. It invents on its own, not under social pressure, which is the exact inverse of the registered prediction. The successor tier ran the probe clean and pushes back on wrong tempo and meter (deference 4/11 and 3/11), though it still swallows the wrong key 10 of 11. The registered availability probe answered the swap question structurally: gpt-4o-audio-preview is not on the gateway and no Anthropic model takes audio, so the swap space for this surface is gemini-only.

body.heading: Honest Accounting
body.html: The registered scorecard ran mostly against the predictions: 1 wrong in the instructive direction (the invented tempo came unprompted, not under false authority); 2 half-right (meter weak blind, candidates only partially fix it); 3 wrong (deference was highest for key, not meter, and production deferred on everything); 4 right (the chart lifts change detection to 6 of 6, placed); 5 wrong (one octave error, not two, because the blind misses were prior-pinning, not octave confusion). Total spend about $1.20 of the $13 in fences, with both discarded pilots archived with their anatomy.

body.heading: What This Licenses
body.html: For Stem Shovel, briefed back to the app the same day: never let the second opinion override the DSP detector on tempo or meter; gate or shrink the no-chart path, since a blind listen adds fabrication risk for no measured value; ignore the confidence field, which reads 1.0 on fabricated answers; and treat the song-check as a chart-anchoring tool, where it is measured perfect. For everyone else: an audio-capable model that answers confidently about a mix is most likely reading the text you sent with it, and the cheapest way to know is a fixture whose pulse you can prove. Stem Shovel rebuilt the feature on this guidance, and Study 7 re-measured the redesign: the deference failure is closed.

studies.title: The composed pipeline: the chain adds nothing of its own, and its first run audited its own predecessors
studies.eyebrow: Study 5 · composition · 48 fresh cells against a frozen ceiling
studies.indexLine: Production composes chart-read and the song-check: the chart beside the mix is the reader's imperfect output, not truth. Study 5 measured the composed chain against Study 4's frozen ceiling with a committed propagation classifier, and its first run's anatomy caught a cross-study confound in the bench's own PDF generation, forcing the Study 3 correction. On honest pages both gates pass at zero listener-added errors, the propagation table is 37 pass and 1 rescued per arm, and the one fact the reader omitted was rescued by the listener reading the chart's chord content, placing the modulation at 20.2 seconds against a 20.21-second truth.

body.heading: The Question
body.html: Studies 3 and 4 measured chart-read and the song-check separately, and separately they are solved problems: a frontier reader at 98.8% and a listener that is perfect when the chart is in view. But production composes them, and the chart beside the mix is chart-read's imperfect output, not the truth Study 4 supplied. Study 5 measured the composed chain: Study 4's 12 metered mixes, their matching lead sheets engraved by Study 3's committed pipeline, read by production's chart-read in both input formats, and the reader's output fed to production's song-check in place of truth, with Study 4's frozen chart-arm cells as the registered ceiling and a committed propagation classifier sorting every fact into pass, listener-added, propagated, rescued or mutated.

body.heading: The Study That Audited Its Own Predecessors
body.html: The first run's biggest result was upstream of the study: the PDF-arm reader kept reporting chords with no flats, and the mechanism check proved the bench's own PDF generation was the culprit, pdfkit's WinAnsi fonts silently dropping the music accidental glyphs Verovio writes into chord text, in every committed PDF of this study and Study 3 alike. The composed chain, built to detect error propagation, caught a fixture confound its predecessor had published numbers on. Amendment 1 committed the finding, the affected cells were discarded and archived, the PDFs re-rendered with ASCII accidentals, and Study 3's Correction was issued the same day. One classifier disclosure rode along: a reader's positional error converts downstream into a confidently wrong second-placement that the value-level extraction attributes to the listener, so the analysis reports position propagation explicitly.

body.heading: The Corrected Verdict
body.html: On honest pages, both gates pass with zero listener-added errors. Across 38 facts per arm the reader made exactly one error, omitting one score's relative-major modulation line from its summary, and the listener rescued it in both arms: reading the chart's chord content (the progression turns to C material), it reported the modulation anyway and placed it at 20.2 seconds against a 20.21-second truth. That rescue is the composed chain's one addition over its parts, and it runs in the right direction. Nothing propagated, nothing mutated: 37 pass and 1 rescued, per arm, against a frozen ceiling the chain equals.

body.heading: What the Confounded Run Showed
body.html: The discarded first run earns its own record, because it demonstrated the failure mode the corrected run no longer could: the chain faithfully transmitting upstream damage. Shown a B-minor sheet whose F#7 printed as F7, the reader reasonably named D major and the listener propagated it one to one; the reader's positional misreadings converted into confidently wrong second-placements downstream. The chain did not amplify or dampen any of it. The corrected run shows none of these, for the simple reason that the pages stopped lying.

body.heading: The Composition Law
body.html: Both runs together give the honest composition story: the chain adds nothing of its own. With a competent reader on honest pages it equals its ceiling; fed corrupted pages it transmits the corruption at full confidence. The quality of the composed feature is exactly the quality of the page its reader is shown, which makes the reader's input, not the chain's plumbing, the thing worth engineering.

body.heading: What This Licenses
body.html: For Stem Shovel: the song-check inherits chart-read's accuracy one to one, so surfacing the chart summary for user correction protects everything downstream of it, and the production model's unprompted key-vs-chords inconsistency notes deserve treatment as a first-class signal rather than prose, since they are the one detectable trace of unrecoverable upstream corruption. Total spend about $3.40 of the $6 fence, both runs included, with the confounded cells archived rather than deleted. The warning heuristic that grew from this study's confound was validated in Study 6, closing the loop a second time.

body.heading: The Loop, Closing Twice
body.html: Study 5 caught the bench's own PDF renderer dropping accidentals; the correction brief suggested a production guard; Stem Shovel shipped it as chartReadWarnings (flag a read whose key signature calls for two or more accidentals while none of eight or more chord symbols carries one). Study 6 is the bench validating the production feature that exists because of the bench's own correction, and it cost nothing to run: the corpus already held 148 reader texts of the same engraved pages, 52 from corrupted PDFs and 96 from clean ones, with expected labels mechanical from the committed specs. The program's first zero-model-spend study.

body.heading: Three Instruments, One Table
body.html: The shipped rule works where it matters: 10 of 10 detectable corrupted reads fired. Its false-positive class is exactly the one its own source comment worries about, now measured at 4 of 42 clean production-reader cells: honest sharp-key charts whose chords legitimately carry no accidentals trip the all-or-nothing rule. The registered refinement (count only chords on the signature's own altered letters) removes that class and exposes one the registration did not predict: modulating charts, where pooling signatures across sections makes one key's honest naturals look suspicious against another key's letters. An exploratory key-in-force variant, disclosed as post-hoc, judges each chord against the signature active at its measure and resolves both classes at 1 of 42, and its single surviving flag is the best result in the study: it fired on a read whose modulation was placed three bars late, a genuine defect flagged for the wrong stated reason. The misses on undetectable reads are floor effects, stub reads that never reach eight chords, per the registered prediction.

body.heading: The Recommendation, and the Scorecard
body.html: Briefed back to Stem Shovel: adopt key-in-force scoping, re-validated on the app's side or a registered extension since the bench's variant is exploratory, and soften the warning's stated cause, because the evidence says the flag earns trust as review-this-read generally, covering both file corruption and a doubtful read. Scorecard: predictions 1 and 3 right, 2 half-right (the predicted fix worked; the modulation class was not predicted). Zero model spend, both registered instruments and the label derivation committed and tested before evaluation. Stem Shovel shipped the recommendation, then registered its own validation of it, and the rule survived on unseen data: Study 6b.

body.heading: The Redesign Inventory
body.html: Study 4 found the song-check echoing whatever candidates rode beside the audio, and Stem Shovel rebuilt the feature in response: the prompt reframes the model as a chart reader, adds an explicit instruction never to estimate a tempo by ear, presents the song's settings as bar-following facts rather than candidates to confirm or correct, applies answers through a chartStatedAnswer gate that only keeps fields the chart actually states, and deletes the confidence field Study 4 showed reading 1.0 on fabrications. Study 7 measured the replacement: the v0.192.0 call ported verbatim and pinned, four arms over Study 4's truth-by-construction mixes, crossing a tempo-stating score summary against a chord-only band chart (a committed generator whose no-tempo, no-meter property is asserted by test) with true against wrong settings. Two gemini generations, 96 cells, about $0.40 of the $5 fence, graded at two levels: the raw answer and what the gate lets through.

body.heading: The Deference Failure Is Closed
body.html: S7-G1 passes decisively. Zero wrong settings survived to application on the production model, 0 of 24 per field, against the retired design's anchor of 10 to 12 of 12 echoed straight into the answer. The raw number underneath is the stronger result: told the song's settings say tempo 240 while the chart's mark reads 120, the model follows the chart, 12 of 12, before any gate touches the answer. When there is a chart statement to transcribe, the chart-transcription framing simply works.

body.heading: The Instruction Loses to the Text, Fourth Appearance
body.html: S7-G2 fails at 24 of 24, and the values convict the mechanism beyond argument. On chord-only charts, where no tempo mark exists anywhere and the registered correct answer is null, the model never answered null, and it did not estimate by ear either: every single invented tempo equals the settings value verbatim. 120 in, 120 out; a lying 60 in, 60 out; both models, 47 of 47 cells, and meter behaves identically. The instruction says use the settings to follow the bars; the model reads that as this is the tempo; and when instruction and text contradict, the text wins. That is the program's recurring law in its fourth costume, after the hint-following of Study 1, the call shapes of Study 2, and the candidates of Study 4. Study 8 adds the corollary from the section detector: the chart's text beats wrong settings, and the chart's silence does not beat the model's priors.

body.heading: Harm Containment, and the Guard's Design Limit
body.html: Nothing wrong can reach a song: chartStatedAnswer nulls tempo and meter on a chart that states neither, 24 of 24 correct refusals, so the study gate fails by letter while its harm is fully contained, a shape this program has learned to read precisely. The guard's design limit also surfaced, once, on the successor model: 3.5-flash echoed a wrong setting under a truth-stating chart, and the presence-based gate (the chart states a tempo, so keep the model's) passed the wrong value through, 1 of 22. The production model never did, and the gate is production-scoped, so G1 stands; the leak names the next refinement, substitution by value rather than filtering by presence.

body.heading: What Still Works, and What Degrades
body.html: The band-chart path's actual job measured perfect: key from chords alone, 12 of 12 on both models. And the registered degradation prediction held exactly: keyChange placement under wrong-tempo bar-following inherits the lie, falling from 3 of 3 to 1 of 3 on the production model and to 0 of 3 on 3.5-flash, because converting bars to seconds with a wrong tempo is just arithmetic on a false premise.

body.heading: Ship Guidance, and the Scorecard
body.html: Briefed back to Stem Shovel: never display raw tempo or meter from chord-path answers, since the applied nulls are the real result; and the deeper fix is structural, because the chart summary's tempo marks and time signature are machine-readable text, so tempo and meter need no model at all. Parse them straight from the chart, substitute by value in the gate, and reserve the model for what measured perfect: keys from chords and placement in seconds. The scorecard: prediction 1 half-right, 2 wrong in both directions at once (score-chart echo fell to zero AND chord-chart echo rose to everything, the split being the finding the prediction missed), 3 right in both halves, 4 wrong, with the production model out-resisting its successor under the new prompt.

studies.indexLine: Section detection was the last unmeasured AI feature, and the loophole test: Studies 4 and 7 showed the listening layer reads rather than hears, but what it did register blind were gross structural events, and section boundaries are gross structural events. The loophole is real: blind texture-contrast boundaries landed 7/8 and 8/8 across two models, the program's first genuine listening result. But the hearing is texture, not form: harmonic boundaries landed 3/6, uniform loops gained three to six invented sections each, and the gate failed by half a false boundary (noise 0.53 per item against a 0.50 bound) even though chart-anchored detection was perfect, because the chart's silence does not beat the model's form prior.

body.heading: The Loophole Test
body.html: Every listening verdict so far said the models read rather than hear, but Studies 4 and 7 both left one loophole on the record: what the listener did register blind were gross structural events, a tempo double noticed in prose, a texture shift remarked on. Section boundaries ARE gross structural events, and section detection was the last AI feature in the app without a measurement. Study 8 ported the v0.192.0 detectSectionsWithAi call verbatim and extended Study 4's fixture with three sparse-and-dense contrast mixes, boundaries a human hears instantly, names and seconds true by construction, then ran three arms: blind, with the account's section vocabulary, and with the marked chart. Two gemini generations, 90 cells, about $0.60 of the fence.

body.heading: Amendment 1: Our Own Study 2 Shape
body.html: Before publication, the bench caught itself in the exact shape Study 2 caught in kimi: the harness's 2000-token output cap truncated the rambling production model mid-JSON in 16 cells, conflating budget exhaustion with failure. The cap was raised to 4000 and the failed cells re-run, disclosed and committed before any result was read. Two production-model cells never produced JSON at any budget; they are counted as misses, disclosed rather than excluded.

body.heading: The Loophole Is Real
body.html: On the contrast mixes, blind, the production model found 7 of 8 section boundaries and 3.5-flash found 8 of 8. After four consecutive studies whose listening verdicts were text-reading verdicts, this is the program's first genuine hearing result: a sparse-to-dense arrangement change is something the audio stack actually registers, without a word of text to transcribe.

body.heading: Texture, Not Form
body.html: The hearing stops at texture. Harmonic and tempo-change boundaries, the kind that define musical form without an arrangement change, landed 3 of 6 blind. And uniform single-section loops, the sharpest probe, were subdivided into invented verse-and-chorus structure at three to six false boundaries per item. The generational split runs opposite to Study 4's equality: 3.5-flash is much cleaner blind (1.0 false boundaries per item against the production model's 3.3), so structural hearing is improving across generations even while neither model can be called a form listener.

body.heading: The Gate, Lost by Half a Boundary, and the Chart-Silence Corollary
body.html: S8-G1 fails by the narrowest margin in the program: chart-anchored detection was perfect, 14 of 14 boundaries with every placement within 4 seconds, but mean false boundaries landed at 0.53 per item against the registered 0.50 bound, eight false boundaries across fifteen items where the bound allowed seven and a half. 3.5-flash passes at 0.47. The noise source is the finding's sharpest nuance: even chart-anchored, uniform loops gain about 1.2 invented boundaries per item while contrast and change items sit at zero, because the chart's single rehearsal mark does not stop the form prior from inventing a chorus. Study 7 established that explicit chart text beats wrong settings; Study 8's corollary is that the chart's silence does not beat the model's priors. Names complete the pattern: 8 of 8 from the chart, 3 of 8 or worse without, because names come from text, as everything always has.

body.heading: Ship Guidance, and the Scorecard
body.html: Briefed back to Stem Shovel: ship section detection chart-gated like the song-check; a surviving blind mode is honest only for arrangement-contrast boundaries and should say so in its copy; and the parse-dont-ask rule extends here, taking the section count and names mechanically from the chart's rehearsal marks and asking the model only for what measured perfect and text cannot supply, the boundaries' placement in seconds, which zeros the loop subdivision by construction and passes the gate without re-registering it. The scorecard: prediction 1 wrong by letter (100% detection, gate lost on noise), 2 substantially right, 3 mixed (vocabulary moved little), 4 wrong in the instructive direction. Study 9 then found the structural fix: a zero-cost per-stem activity detector that cannot invent a boundary on a loop by construction.

body.heading: The Production Agent Registers Its Own Test
body.html: Study 6 validated Stem Shovel's warning heuristic and recommended a key-in-force refinement, flagged honestly as exploratory. Stem Shovel shipped the refinement, then did the thing the program exists to teach: it declined to trust its own shipped rule, on the stated ground that a rule designed on the data it is scored on fits that data, and registered its own validation in the bench. Study 6b is that registration, run by the bench without adjustment, which makes cross-agent registration a two-way street for the first time: the bench has audited the product for weeks, and now the product audits itself through the bench.

body.heading: Four Safeguards, Then a Perfect Sheet
body.html: The design carries four registered safeguards: new-data quarantine (24 charts the rule had never seen, engraved clean and corrupted through a registered generator option, with each of Study 6's named false-positive classes represented 8 items strong); a verbatim port of the shipped rule pinned at its own commit; a tested only-quieter property between the shipped rule and the bench's exploratory variant; and a zero-spend reproduction check gating the run, which reproduced Study 6's numbers exactly before any new read was scored. On the production reader the sheet came back perfect: 8 of 8 detectable corrupted reads caught, 16 of 16 undetectable reads silent, 0 of 24 clean reads flagged, with zeros in the modulating-chart class where the pooled rule failed and the honest sharp-key class where the pre-refinement rule failed. The extra condition added at productionization cost nothing, and all four registered predictions held. About $1.60 of the $6 cap.

body.heading: The Longest Loop Closes
body.html: The verdict delivered back to the app: nothing to change. The loop this closes is the program's longest, four hand-offs with each side checking the other: Study 5's anatomy found the corruption class, Study 3's correction described it, Stem Shovel shipped a heuristic, Study 6 measured it and suggested the refinement, Stem Shovel shipped the refinement and registered its own validation, and Study 6b confirms it on data it was not designed on: 100% hit, 100% silence, zero false alarms.

body.heading: Drafted by the App, Run by the Bench
body.html: Study 6b was registered by the production agent; Study 9 runs the collaboration the other way, drafted by the Stem Shovel agent and finished, registered, and run by the bench. The question is the app's own: it holds the individual stems of every song, yet its detector and both AI features analyze the summed mix, so does stem-aware analysis beat the sum? Four zero-model-spend DSP instruments ran over 21 items (the 15 pulsed Study 4 and 8 specs plus 6 new misleading-stem specs whose fourth part, a rubato lead, an off-grid pad, a noise and room track, or a double-time comp, is designed to pollute the summed onset envelope), with stems shuffled so no instrument knows which is the drums. D-prod is a verbatim port of production's analysis code, pinned at its commit. A 12-call AI side arm rode along; total spend about $0.08.

body.heading: The Form Half: a Detector That Cannot Invent
body.html: S9-G1 passed perfectly on both the truth bar grid and the production-portable detected grid: D-activity, which marks a boundary where the set of active stems changes and holds for two bars, found 8 of 8 contrast boundaries with zero false boundaries on the uniform loops and the change items alike. Set beside Study 8's results on the same items, the shape is the point: models blind invented 3 to 6 sections per loop, the chart-anchored production model still invented about one, and the activity detector invents nothing because on a loop the active set never changes; the failure mode is excluded by construction, not suppressed by a bound. Its blindness is equally structural: all six tempo and key-change boundaries, where the arrangement does not change, are invisible to it, as registered; those belong to the chart. One honest caveat from the mislead class: a noise track with slow swells toggles its own activity bit (two false boundaries on one item), so a shipped version wants the atonal-stem guard.

body.heading: The Time Half: the Failure Is the Finding
body.html: S9-G2 failed decisively, and the failure is the study's most useful result. Keeping the sharpest single stem's tempo instead of the sum's does not help; it harms: D-prod exact on 18 of 21 items, the sharpest-stem rule on 11 of 21, with 7 regressions (5 of them octave errors, because a clean bass line autocorrelates beautifully at half time) and zero rescues. Meanwhile the summed envelope survived all six misleading extras untouched: pad, noise, rubato, and both double-time comps left it exact. Summing the stems is not a compromise production settled for; the cross-stem reinforcement at the true period IS the tempo signal, and the shipped design is vindicated against every stem-aware variant tried. The sum's only misses are a shared systematic, the 3:2 dotted-pulse confusion on compound meters, which no stem-aware variant fixed either. The registered octave-disagreement flag fired on 10 of 21 items including clean ones, a half-time bass being normal music rather than a hazard signal, and is reported as measured: useless as shipped.

body.heading: The Key Sting
body.html: S9-G3 was unevaluable under its registered fallback, since production's key detection was right on 20 of 21 items and there was nothing to separate. The descriptive warning that rode along is worth the section: the one wrong answer carried a per-stem agreement score of 1.00, the maximum, while production's own correlation margin ranked that same answer third-lowest of 21. On this corpus the proposed agreement score did not merely fail to prove itself; it pointed the wrong way on the only error available, while the existing confidence pointed the right way.

body.heading: The Pilot, and the Familiar Prior
body.html: The 12-call pilot gave gemini-3-flash the isolated bass and comp stem in place of the mix. It helped nowhere and hurt twice, with two items flipping from right to wrong, and the tempo answers were the familiar 120, 126, 128 genre prior in both conditions: Study 4's reading-not-hearing, unchanged by stem isolation. The registered prediction said at most one item would change; two did, both for the worse, direction right and count wrong. The fenced matrix stays open but unneeded, since the gates did not require it.

body.heading: Ship Guidance, and the Scorecard
body.html: Briefed back to Stem Shovel: ship nothing for tempo and key, since the summed-envelope detector beat every stem-aware variant and its one weakness is not fixed by stems; and consider shipping D-activity as a browser-side section detector, zero model cost, structurally immune to the loop invention that survived even chart anchoring in Study 8, guarded against sustained-noise stems, with the model kept for names and the chart for harmonic boundaries. The scorecard: prediction 1 right in full, 2 refuted in both halves, 3 right except the agreement-floor guess (the real floor was indifference to the one actual error), 4 right in direction and wrong in count. One suggestion here did not survive its next test: Study 10's real-recording rematch dropped D-activity to 25/33 with 19 false boundaries on real stems, and the measured no-chart section fallback is now the LinkSeg segmenter. The correction is stated plainly there.

body.heading: Drafted From the Landscape, Verified by the Bench
body.html: The third cross-agent study: the Stem Shovel agent drafted it from its own landscape review, asking whether the app hears with obsolete code, and the bench finished and registered it after verifying that the three cited HuggingFace ONNX models exist with hashes matching their published tables. The candidates: Beat This! small (MIT) for tempo and meter, LinkSeg 7-class (CC-BY 4.0) for sections, ChordMini (MIT) for chords, plus two literature key-profile swaps; one published tracker was omitted on licensing (its library is CC BY-NC-SA). Runners are vendored reference code; the fixture adds a 12-item hard set (swing, octave-boundary tempi, reverb, dense mixes, mediant modulations) and 4 extended-chord progressions. Zero LLM spend in both arms.

body.heading: Five Gates, Five Fails, All in Production's Favor
body.html: The synthetic arm's verdict is uniform: every registered gate failed in the shipped code's favor. The beat gate carries the study's most instructive nuance: at the registered plus-or-minus 1 bpm, production is exact on 29 of 33 to the neural tracker's 18, but the tracker derives tempo from a 20 ms frame grid, so it answers 142.9 for a true 140, musically right and numerically outside the letter; a disclosed sensitivity read at plus-or-minus 3 is a dead tie at 29 each, the program's fifth registration lesson (an absolute tolerance at DSP precision measures the candidate's output quantization, not its hearing). What the letter cannot take away: the tracker's per-beat grid scores an F-measure of 0.892, something production does not have at all, and it answered the pulseless pads honestly. Meter went 27/29 to 21/29 for production, with the hoped-for free 6/8 dead at 1 of 4; and the key profiles tied on synthetic material (29, 29, 30 of 33), deferring the real question to the amendment.

body.heading: The Segmenter and the Chord Reader
body.html: The section gate failed decisively: LinkSeg placed 54 false boundaries across the 22 single-section items, about 2.5 per item, worse than Study 8's chart-anchored language models, while finding only 5 of 8 contrast boundaries; graph attention does not cure the loop-invention disease on this fixture, where Study 9's free activity detector scored 8 of 8 with zero. The chord gate split: the production matcher took the full vocabulary 483 to 418 of 504 bars (the neural model hears triads where the truth says sevenths), ChordMini edged the hard set on major-minor nuance 61 to 59 of 64, and one collapse earns its name: the N.C.-bar song fell to 4 of 28 under the neural reader while the matcher read 27. Deployment was never the blocker; every candidate fit the size and latency budget, and accuracy decided everything.

body.heading: The Home-Field Rematch
body.html: The registered real-recordings amendment ran the same day on a public catalog of the band's own songs, scored against the band's declarations, including declared section start seconds. The domain warning was real, in both directions. Sections flip outright: LinkSeg finds real form at 29 of 33 declared boundaries within 4 seconds, including one song at 8 of 9 with zero false boundaries, while Study 9's D-activity, perfect on synthetic arrangements, drops to 25 of 33 with 19 false boundaries on real stems. That is a plain correction of Study 9's ship suggestion, and this page says so: the measured no-chart section fallback is now the 1.5 MB CC-BY segmenter, not the bench's own detector. Tempo kept its known shape with real teeth: production's two misses are gross, an exact half of a declared 224 and an exact two-thirds of a declared 145, the 3:2 family on real recordings, while the neural tracker leads 3 of 4 at the wider read (n of 4, direction not proof) by degrading gracefully instead of octave-jumping. Meter held for production, which read the real waltz the tracker missed. And the key question closed hard: Krumhansl 4 of 6 against 1 of 6 for both literature profiles, which collapse into parallel-minor and subdominant flips on real mixes. The synthetic arm said interchangeable; the real arm says production's choice is the right one.

body.heading: Ship Guidance
body.html: Briefed back to Stem Shovel: nothing ships for tempo, since the detector's failure classes are known and the neural alternative is not plus-or-minus-1 accurate on real material either; keep Krumhansl without a second thought; and consider LinkSeg, behind the chart when one exists, as the no-chart section fallback that the real recordings earned it. The honest boundary runs both ways and is stated in the report: the synthetic corpus is the material production's templates were born on, and the real catalog is the material the neural models were trained for; both arms exist precisely so neither home field decides alone.

body.heading: The Scorecard, and the Ledger
body.html: The registered scorecard ran against the draft's hopes: prediction 3 right in full including the one-profile detail, 1 wrong at the registered letter and right at the disclosed wider read, 2 wrong in both clauses, 4 wrong except the hard-set edge, 5 half-right with the zero-false clause failing much harder than predicted, 6 wrong in the happy direction. body.heading: Retire the Error by Representation
body.html: Five studies built the same file on the detector's one recurring failure: the octave family, a clean bass heard at half time, a 6/8 lilt read at 3:2. Study 11 runs the fix the Stem Shovel agent specified in its review of the bench's tempo-grid proposal: stop asking the detector to hear better, and represent its answer as a rung on an octave ladder, with a gate deciding which rungs a declared tempo may legitimately match and a subdivision test deciding duple against triple at a named hypothesis. The bench registered it with three disclosed restatements (production's shipped 2 percent ratio rule in place of an absolute tolerance, one item in the six-miss list corrected to the detector's own misses, and one gate redefined off Study 7's cells, whose registered wrong settings are octave-rung values by construction). Zero model spend: two pure functions over the stored Study 10 detections, 37 items, 255 mechanically wrong declared values, three runs.

body.heading: Two Instrument Defects, Caught and Amended Before Any Result
body.html: The first runs caught two defects in the measuring instruments, both fixed by registered amendment and both findings in their own right. The slower-of-pair subdivision hypothesis is mathematically confounded: a straight song misread at two-thirds maps its true duple eighths exactly onto the slower pulse's thirds, so the test read compound on the one item it exists to reject; the hypothesis became the declared tempo, the claim actually under test. And at a bogus hypothesis tempo there is no beat peak at all, so the relative floor goes vacuous and 22 of 33 wrong rows were licensed; a beat floor now requires the hypothesis pulse to exist, three orders of magnitude of separation in the data, on the principle that a compound-count claim about a pulse that does not exist is no claim.

body.heading: The Gates That Passed
body.html: G1, 5 of 5 plus the rejection that matters: both lilts, the 3/4 contrast item and the reverb item recover at the two-thirds rung on genuine compound evidence, the double-time song recovers at rung 2, and peaceful-dreams, the true hearing error the specification insisted must stay an error, is correctly refused by the gated ladder while the open ladder accepts it. G3, clean: subdivision reads 3 on all four compound items and 2 on all 31 straight items outside the swing pair, which splits honestly (a 0.67 swing ratio reads as a 3-feel because triplet swing is one; 0.62 reads 2), and the derived meter names 6/8 on every compound item, the first time the detector's vocabulary has been able to say it.

body.heading: The Gates That Failed, on Their Own Measuring Stick
body.html: G2 failed by letter at 1 of 33, and the one accepted row is a true value: the generator built a wrong 108 from the first section's 72 on a song whose own second section is declared at 108. G4 failed by letter at 1 of 221, a pairing artifact: wrongness was defined against truth while the comparison runs against the detection, and on the one item where the detection itself was 3:2-off, the truth-derived wrong value lands on the double rung of the wrong grid. Across all 255 rows, zero genuinely wrong values were accepted, and the open ladder's 30 of 33 acceptances are the measured justification for gating. The sixth registration lesson, earned twice in one study: a mechanical wrong-value generator must respect every true label of an item, and define wrongness against the value actually being compared.

body.heading: The Shipping Question, and What Stays Pending
body.html: The specification's own decision rule anticipated a full pass or a failed gate; neither branch matches two by-letter failures that transfer to the generator rather than the rule. Per program discipline the gates are not re-thresholded; the bench's read, on the table for Stem Shovel's call, is that the evidence supports the full build list, with a corrected generator a one-line registered follow-up. One thing this page deliberately does not claim: Stem Shovel built the ship items while the study ran, with a sharper subdivision rule than the sketch the bench tested, and that shipped rule is not validated by this study. The bench has committed to a follow-up validation of the shipped rule plus a swing-stress set once its commit lands, and until then it is pending, stated as such. That follow-up has now run: Study 11b validates the shipped rule's triplet share and ladder outright, and finds the compound flag carried this study's Amendment 1 confound into production.

body.heading: The Scorecard, and the Thread
body.html: The registered scorecard: prediction 1 right in full, 2 right in direction and wrong by letter through the generator collision, 3 right including the swing split, 4 wrong by letter through the pairing artifact it did not anticipate. Zero dollars, three runs, all local arithmetic, superseded runs kept in history. The thread Studies 4, 7, 8, 9 and 10 built closes on its intended note: the octave error class is retired not by a better ear but by a better representation of what the ear already says.

body.heading: The Ladder Thread Closes Like the Warning Thread Did
body.html: Study 6b set the pattern: the production side ships, declines to trust its own work, and asks the bench to validate it. The ladder thread now ends the same way. Stem Shovel built the tempo ladder in production (v0.200.0) in parallel with Study 11, with a sharper subdivision rule than the sketch the bench had tested, and requested validation of the shipped rule verbatim plus a swing-stress sweep. The bench ported it pinned at their commit and ran 52 detector reads (the Study 11 corpus, the real recordings, and 15 new swing-stress items at ratios 0.60 to 0.70 across three tempi) plus 332 wrong-tempo rows through the lesson-six-corrected generator. Zero spend, one disclosed pre-registration smoke, and a thread ledger worth a line: the four ladder-thread studies together cost about eight cents of model spend, all of it Study 9's pilot.

body.heading: What Validates Clean
body.html: V3 passed 15 of 15: not one swing item at any ratio or tempo read compound, every tempo exact, validating the shipped TRIPLET_SHARE of 0.55 and its swing-cannot-exceed-half argument across the full sweep, including the 0.67 triplet swing the bench's own sketch rule had misread. V4 passed 0 of 332 false accepts through the corrected generator, which also retro-confirms Study 11's reading that its by-letter failures were generator collisions rather than ladder defects. And the shipped super-beat re-pick fixed two of Study 10's octave-family misses outright: two 6/8 items now detect their dotted tempo exactly at the detector level.

body.heading: The Margin That Cannot Be Tuned
body.html: V1 failed 2 of 4, and the margin numbers are the point: they forbid the obvious fix. lilt-a's super-beat ratio is 1.029 against the shipped 1.05 margin (the app's own fixtures measured 1.02 to 1.12; the bench's lighter accents land at the bottom of that band), and verb-y's reverb smears its ratio to 0.991, down among the straight items' own ratios (their published band runs 0.91 to 0.97), where no margin reaches it without letting straight songs through. The distributions overlap, so lowering the margin trades missed 6/8 for false 6/8. The save is complete, though: on all four compound items the true dotted tempo sits on the shipped alternates ladder at top-rung strength, so the rung-picker surfaces the right count everywhere the automatic call misses.

body.heading: The Confound Shipped
body.html: V2 is the finding that matters: both scorable real recordings flipped to 6/8. mop-heart re-picked to 74.7, which is exactly the declared 224 divided by three, the bar pulse of a fast waltz counted in one: a musically defensible hearing with no rung to land on, since 224 matched the old detection at rung 2 and matches nothing on the new ladder, which lacks a times-3 rung. And peaceful-dreams' sub-beat test fired at the detector's own two-thirds-wrong pulse, which is Study 11 Amendment 1's confound, now in shipped code: at the wrong pulse, a third of the lag IS the true eighth note, the test is structurally unable to tell compound-here from straight-at-1.5x-of-here, and the shipped ladder then matched the declared 145 on the detector's own confounded flag. The warning that Study 11's gates required to stay loud goes silent, for the wrong reason.

body.heading: Verdict, and the Scorecard
body.html: The verdict delivered to Stem Shovel: keep the triplet share, the ladder util, and the re-pick as shipped; evaluate the compound flag at the DECLARED tempo's lag, the Amendment 1 rule, which cleanly separates the genuine compound item (0.72 at its declared lag) from the confounded one (0.03); add the times-3 rung or a 3/4-in-one expression; and do not lower the margin, since one item proves the bands overlap. Not a stop-ship: the false fires on declared-straight real songs are contained by the flag fix at the warning surface, and the alternates carry the truth. The scorecard: prediction 1 half-right (the re-pick works more often than the smoke suggested), 2 wrong in the instructive direction (both real recordings flipped, the exact risk the addendum named where it said to stress), 3 and 4 right in full. Stem Shovel answered with a patch that moved both gates to the declared meter, rejected the bench's proposed flag fix with a counterexample, and requested the validations that became Study 11c, where the patch validated and the bench's own rule was retired on the record.

body.heading: The Patch, the Rejection, and the Registered Defeat

body.heading: The Gate That Strictly Dominates
body.html: C1 passed perfectly: over the full 11b corpus, the declared-meter gate accepted 0 of 332 corrected wrong rows, lost no true-count match, and GAINED three over the shipped v0.200.0 rule. The two compound items the acoustic margin had missed now match at two-thirds through their declared 6/8, and the fast waltz matches at times-3 through its declared 3/4: 224, counted three to the bar. The one item that must stay an error stays loud, now by data instead of by luck. C3 passed as cleanly: the new rung opens nowhere but declared-triple meters, zero leaks, zero off-tolerance accepts, with the count ambiguity quantified and living where it belongs, in the rung picker.

body.heading: The Mirror Did Its Job Twice Over
body.html: C2 is the study's heart. The bench's declared-lag rule accepted 3 of 3 wrong mirror values, exactly as the registered prediction traced: on straight running eighths, a two-thirds-wrong declared tempo puts its lag's third on the eighth grid, and every clause of the bench's amended rule licenses the rung, beat floor included. The bench's own proposed rule is retired on the record, by the measurement its proposer registered. The letter of the gate failed on the other half (the declared-meter side accepted 1 of 3), and the anatomy deserves plain statement: on the 138 bpm mirror the DETECTOR itself misread the straight eighths at 92 with a false compound flag, and the wrong declared 92 then matched the wrong detection directly at rung 1, which no gate governs. A ladder cannot reject declared-equals-detected; this is Study 11's lesson-six collision class again, not a gate leak, and the gates themselves never opened.

body.heading: The Bonus Fixture
body.html: The mirror incidentally built the first SYNTHETIC reproduction of the detection-side confound: truth 138, detected 92 with a false compound flag, the true tempo sitting on the alternates at strength 0.96. The confound that previously existed only on one real recording now has a committed regression fixture, and the patched comparison surface already contains it correctly: the declared-meter gate refuses to call 138-against-92 a count, so the warning stays loud.

body.heading: Verdict, Scorecard, and the Thread's Ledger
body.html: The verdict delivered: ship the patch to production as is. The declared-meter gate strictly dominates both its predecessors on everything a gate controls, and the one C2 accept is detection-side and pre-existing, with mirror-138 as its new regression fixture. The scorecard: prediction 1 right in full, 2 half (the bench's defeat traced exactly, the collision-class accept unanticipated), 3 right in full. body.heading: The Arc-Closer, the Bench's Own Registration
body.html: Study 8 left exactly one hearing job with the language model: placing section boundaries in seconds. Study 12, the candidates memo's recommendation A, registered by the bench and approved for its zero spend, takes it with code: render the chart as sustained chord pads at the declared tempo, knowing nothing the chart does not state; compute a 92.9 ms chromagram on the port's own FFT; and align render to recording with dynamic time warping, non-stalling reference steps, and a subsequence mode for count-ins and tails. The corpora: 33 synthetic items with truth by construction, a six-pair wrong-chart probe, and the bench's disclosed transcriptions of the public Badverbs charts, scoped honestly: one song gated (unambiguous, duration cross-checked), one exploratory with a disclosed 26-second reading mismatch, and one excluded as untranscribable, which is itself the real-world limit of chart-driven anything.

body.heading: Bars to the Hop
body.html: G1a passed at exactly the letter: 532 of 560 synthetic bar starts, 95.0 percent, within a quarter second. The errors live where physics says they should, in reverb tails (worst 1.3 to 1.4 seconds) and dense mixes, and the mediant modulations, the hard harmonic case, aligned perfectly to the hop.

body.heading: The Precision Every Listener Failed
body.html: G1b is the headline: all eight contrast section boundaries within half a second. That is the precision metric every listener in the program failed, with Study 8's models near zero of eight there, Study 10's neural segmenter at zero of eight, and the literature's best model reader at 0.423 on real music. Beside it, seven of eight tempo and key-change boundaries landed within the same half second, boundaries structurally invisible to stem activity and half-found by blind models, because the warp does not care that the tempo moved. That indifference is the method.

body.heading: The Probe That Replaces an Ear
body.html: The wrong-chart probe separated all six registered pairs, with the right chart's path cost sitting 8.6 to 16.3 times under the wrong one. The is-this-chart-this-recording question, which production currently asks the model to answer by ear in the song check, is now a number with an order-of-magnitude margin.

body.heading: Perfect in the Middle, Lost at the Edges
body.html: G2 failed by one boundary, and the anatomy is the finding. On the real recording, the six mid-song boundaries landed at 0.02 to 0.11 seconds, placement precision nothing in the program has approached on real audio; the three misses are the edges, where the subsequence start absorbs the real intro (3.6 seconds) and the chart's eight-bar outro reading meets a three-second performance tail (9.1 seconds). Alignment is sub-tenth-second wherever the performance follows the chart and fails exactly where the chart stops describing the performance, which is how the neural segmenter edges it seven-to-six at the half-second tolerance on this one song: by being merely mediocre everywhere instead of perfect in the middle and lost at the ends. The exploratory song behaved exactly as predicted, clean until the bench's own uncertain Bridge reading, then two to eight seconds adrift before re-anchoring at the outro: a wrong transcription degrades placement locally and visibly, which is precisely what a shipping gate can catch.

body.heading: Ship Guidance, and the Arc
body.html: Briefed back to Stem Shovel: alignment takes placement, behind two mechanical gates, the path cost (the probe's 8.6-times floor) and an edge flag that shows first and last boundaries hedged, the rung-picker pattern applied again; the probe ships separately as the same-piece check, replacing the by-ear clause; and chart quality is now the binding constraint, a data problem rather than a hearing problem, with one real song untranscribable to make the point. The scorecard: 1 right including the tempo-change tracking, 2 half (the error shape predicted, the count off by one), 3 and 4 right in full. And the arc line the page exists to state: with Study 12, every hearing task measured across the program's twelve stem studies has a code-or-data answer that beats or matches the model, and the models' one genuine hearing ability, texture contrast, was overtaken twice, by stems in Study 9 and by charts here. Study 16 closed the data problem by the fix: with the band's corrected chart, the song this study could only hold as exploratory dropped from a 1.99 second median section error to 0.09 through the production path, confirming that the chart, not the aligner, was the bottleneck.

body.heading: The Conditional Registration
body.html: Would a chord reconciler still have value? Study 13 answers it the way the program has learned to ask: as a registered two-arm conditional, measuring the thing the reconciler would improve first and running the reconciler only if the measurement leaves headroom, with the trigger registered at gated accuracy under 90 percent. Study 12's artifacts made the measurement possible at all, supplying the bar grid in recording seconds and bar-aligned chord truth on real audio. Arm 1 cost nothing; the whole study ran at about $0.60 of its $3 fence.

body.heading: The Home-Field Gap, Measured
body.html: Arm 1 is the finding that matters most: production's chord path, Basic Pitch plus the v0.142 matcher, which scores 95.8 percent at home on the synthetic bench and beat the neural reader in Study 10, reads the real letter-lands recording at 38.2 percent, 29 of 76 bars, with the registered power-chord allowance doing real work on nine of them, and the exploratory song at 27.9 percent. The predicted home-field gap was 15 to 30 points; the measured gap is nearly 60. The binding constraint is the transcription on real timbres, the rich-harmonics weakness Study 1's fixture work warned about, now measured in production conditions instead of suspected. The trigger fired without drama.

body.heading: Amendment 1, the Recurring Own-Harness Lesson
body.html: All four pilot cells truncated at the registered 4000-token output cap, because the models narrate their way through every bar before emitting the JSON: the exact budget-conflates-with-failure class Study 8's amendment caught, back in the bench's own harness. The cap moved to 16,000, the cells re-ran under the fence, and the truncated run stays in history. One more disclosure rode along: the production model ignores the registered temperature-zero deviation, which the gateway reports as unsupported.

body.heading: The Reconciler Earns Its Keep
body.html: Arm 2 passed its gate for both models. One text-only pass over the key, the detected chords and production's own per-bar note lines took the production chart-draft model from 29 to 41 of 76 bars, 53.9 percent: twelve fixes, zero breaks, across 27 changed bars, so the double-fix gate registered against Study 9's agreement trap (fixes must at least double breaks) passed at infinity. gemini-3.5-flash climbed from 29 to 36 with seven fixes and zero breaks. On the exploratory song the production model added three more bars without breaking any, while gemini burned the full 16,000-token budget narrating 86 bars and never reached the JSON, the budget failure mode of that family from Studies 2 and 8, not the over-editing mode the prediction expected.

body.heading: Ship Guidance
body.html: Two findings, delivered in order of weight. First, chord drafts on real user audio are far weaker than any synthetic number suggested, and that reframes the feature's honest quality bar: a UI hedge is worth shipping now, regardless of anything else. Second, the reconciler is real and cheap, a text-only pass by the model production already runs for chart drafts, lifting the real-audio number 16 points with zero breaks for about a cent a song: ship it inside the chart-draft job, symbols in and symbols out, keep the detector's chord whenever the model's answer parses to nothing, and cap output generously. The honest ceiling stands: 54 percent reconciled is better, not good, and if the chord feature matters, the next investment is a stronger transcription on real timbres, not more model. Study 17 has since made that investment and measured it: a zero-model neural front end reads the same recording at 77.6 percent, past this study's reconciled ceiling, and the reconciler stays valid only on the note path that feeds it.

body.heading: The Scorecard, and the Arc Note
body.html: The registered scorecard: 1 right in direction and wrong in magnitude; 2 right, with the changed-bars count just over its sub-claim; 3 wrong in the instructive direction, gemini failing by budget rather than by over-editing; 4 right. The disclosure is Study 1's, unchanged: the analyst is Claude Fable 5 and arm 2 measures claude-fable-5-1, tolerable because every grade is mechanical and committed before any call. And the arc note this page exists to carry: this is the program's first study in which a language model IMPROVED a hearing pipeline, and it did so by never hearing anything, symbols in and symbols out, which is the twelve-study law applied rather than broken.
